source_text: Fragmenta in epistulam i ad Corinthios 1 Kor 15,1-2 Ἐπειδή τινες ἐν Κορίνθῳ ἔλεγον εἶναι τὴν ψυχὴν φθαρτὴν καὶ περιττὴν τὴν τοῦ σώματος ἀνάστασιν, διελέγχει αὐτῶν ὁ Παῦλος τὴν πλάνην, καί φησιν· τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, δι' οὗ ἐκλήθητε ἐκ τῆς πολυθέου πλάνης ἐπὶ τὸ γινώσκειν τὸν ἀληθινὸν θεόν, δι' οὗ βεβαιοῦσθε καὶ σωτηρίαν ἔχετε, γνώριμον ὑμῖν καθίστημι. Τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγέλιον γνωρίζω ὑμῖν, ἵνα εἰδῆτε ὅτι οὐκ ἐμή, ἀλλ' οὔ τινος ἡ περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν μνήμη. 1 Kor 15, 3-4 Παρέδωκέ μοι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ὅτι ἐπιδημήσας ὁ σωτὴρ καὶ σῶμα κατ' ἀλήθειαν φορέσας, ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀναστῆναι τοὺς τεθνεώτας ἀποθανὼν καὶ ταφεὶς ἀνέστη. εἶτα ἵνα μὴ θορυβηθῶσιν οἱ ἁπλούστεροι θάνατον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐπάγει· κατὰ τὰς γραφάς· τοιαῦτα γὰρ πέπονθε ὅσα περὶ αὐτοῦ προανεφώνησαν οἱ προφῆται. ἐπεὶ οὖν ἀπέθανε καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ ἀνέστη, ἀκόλουθόν ἐστιν ἀναστῆναι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ τὸν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀναστάντα, αὐτοῦ αἰτίου γενομένου τῆς ἐγέρσεως. εἰ δὲ λέγεται Χριστὸς τεθνάναι καὶ τεθάφθαι, περὶ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ τοῦτο ἐκληπτέον, οὐ τῆς ψυχῆς. ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐπίστευσαν τῇ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀναστάσει, μεμπταῖοί εἰσι μὴ συμπαραδεξάμενοι τῇ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀναστάσει καὶ τὴν πάντων ἀνάστασιν. 1 Kor 15, 5-9 Ταύτης αὐτοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτόπται ἀξιομάρτυρές εἰσιν οἱ πρῶτοι αὐτῷ συνόντες, ἔπειτα πεντακόσιοι. Ταῦτα, φησί, παραδίδωμι οἷς ἀντειπεῖν οὐ δύνανται οἱ ἀπατῶντες ὑμᾶς. ὅμως, εἰ καὶ τὸ τεθνεὸς σῶμα ἀνίσταται, ἀλλ' ἄφθαρτον καὶ πνευματικόν· διὸ οὐδὲ πᾶσιν ἐφαίνετο ἀλλ' οἷς ἤθελεν. οὕτως μετὰ τὴν ἀνάληψιν ὤφθη τῷ Παύλῳ, ὃς μετριάζων καλεῖ ἑαυτὸν ἔκτρωμα, συναισθόμενος ὅτι ἐκ μετανοίας ἐλήλυθε εἰς τὸ ἀπόστολον εἶναι, καὶ ὡς 7 μηδὲ τῆς ὀνομασίας ἄξιος ὢν ὡς διώκτης. πλὴν εἰ καὶ πάλαι τοιοῦτο, ἀλλὰ νῦν διδάσκαλος ἔχων τοῦτο ἐκ δωρεᾶς. 1 Kor 15, 10-11 Εἰ καὶ πάλαι διώκτης, ἀλλὰ νῦν διδάσκαλος δωρεᾷ θεοῦ ἥτις οὐ ματαίως ἐνυπῆρξεν αὐτῷ, ἐπείπερ ἐνδυναμωθεὶς ὑπ' αὐτῆς περισσοτέρως ἀνέτλη τοὺς ἀγῶνας ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβοῦς πίστεως. ὅλον δὲ τὸ κατόρθωμα ὃ ἔσχεν ἐκ προαιρέσεως, ἀνατίθησι τῇ δοθείσῃ χάριτι θεόθεν αὐτῳ 1 Kor 15, 12-17 Εἴ τις λέγει μὴ ἐγείρεσθαι τοὺς νεκρούς, ἐπειδὴ ἀνάγκη Χριστοῦ ἀναστάντος πάντας ἀνίστασθαι, οὔκουν ἀναγκαίως λέγει μηδὲ Χριστὸν ἐγηγέρθαι; εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἀνέστη, ὅρα πόσα ἀνακύπτει ἄτοπα· ἡμεῖς οἱ εἰπόντες τοῦτο ψευδομάρτυρες εὑρεθησόμεθα κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰ καὶ ὡς ὑμεῖς ἠλιθίως συνέθεσθε τῇ ἐγέρσει τοῦ κυρίου, ἀλλὰ καὶ πίστει τοῦ ἀναστάντος δόξαντες ἠλευθερῶσθαι τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, οὐκ ἀπεβάλετε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν. 1 Kor 15, 18- Ὁ μὴ παραδεξάμενος τὴν ἀνθρώπου ψυχὴν ἀθάνατον εἶναι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀπιστῶν τῇ ἀναστάσει, οἰκτρὸς ὁ τοιοῦτος στερῶν ἑαυτὸν τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς δι' ἣν πλούσιοι οἱ ἅγιοι ἀξίων ἀμοιβῶν τυγχάνοντες. Εἰ καὶ ἀπιστῶσί τινες, ἀλλ' ἡμεῖς προσδοκῶμεν ἀνάστασιν, εἰδότες ὡς ἀπαρχὴ Χριστὸς γέγονεν, ἀνάστασις τῶν κεκοιμημένων· δι' ὧν πάντες πειραθήσονται τῆς ἀθανάτου ζωῆς, ἀκολουθὸν γάρ. 1 Kor 15, 21-22 Ἐπειδὴ διὰ τὸ παραβῆναι τὸν Ἀδὰμ τὸν νόμον οἱ ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες τεθνήκασιν, οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ μὴ γνόντι ἁμαρτίαν ζωοποιηθήσονται. τινὲς δὲ τῶν αἱρετικῶν μόνην λέγουσι τὴν ψυχὴν ζωοποιεῖσθαι ἐν Χριστῷ τῶν δικαίων, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ** ἡ γὰρ ζωοποίησις πάντων ἔσται τῶν ἀποθανόντων ἐν τῷ Ἀδάμ. 1 Kor 15,23-24a Ὡς πρὸ πάντων οὖσα ἡ Χριστοῦ ἀνάστασις, πρώτη ἔσται ἐν τιμῇ· εἶτα ἑξῆς οἱ πιστοὶ κατ' ἀναλογίαν ἧς ἔχουσι πίστεως τάσσονται ἐν τῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ παρουσίᾳ, μεθ' ἣν ἔστιν τὸ τέλος οὕτω πρὸς ἀρχὴν διαστελλόμενον, ἀλλὰ τὸ οὗ εἵνεκα τὰ ἄλλα πάντα τὰ συντείνοντα πρὸς 8 σωτηρίαν, αὐτὸ δὲ οὐκ ἄλλου 1 χάριν ὑπάρχον ἔσχατον ὀρεκτὸν καθ' ἑαυτὸ καὶ δι' ἑαυτὸ αἱρετὸν τυγχάνον.
thought_title: Paul refutes the Corinthians who deny the resurrection
orientation: Didymus opens his commentary on 1 Corinthians 15 by explaining that Paul wrote to correct certain Corinthians who said the soul is perishable and the resurrection of the body is superfluous.
pass_a_gloss: Since certain people in Corinth were saying that the soul is mortal and the resurrection of the body is superfluous, Paul refutes their error and says: the gospel, through which you were called from the polytheistic error to knowing the true God, through which you are made firm and have salvation, I make known to you. I make known to you the gospel of God, so that you may know that the mention of the resurrection of the dead is not mine, nor anyone's. He handed down to me the gospel, that the Savior, having come and having truly worn a body, died and was buried and rose for the sake of the rising of those who have died. Then, so that the simpler ones may not be disturbed at the death of Christ, he adds: according to the scriptures; for he suffered such things as the prophets announced beforehand about him. Since therefore he died and was buried and rose, it follows that human beings rise because of the one who rose for them, he having become the cause of the rising. But if Christ is said to have died and to have been buried, this must be understood about his body, not his soul. Since therefore they believed in the resurrection of the Savior, they are blameworthy for not accepting together with the resurrection of the Savior also the resurrection of all. Eyewitnesses worthy of trust of this resurrection of his are those who were first with him, then five hundred. These things, he says, I hand down, which those who deceive you cannot contradict. Nevertheless, even if the dead rise, yet it is incorruptible and spiritual; therefore it did not appear to all but to those to whom he willed. Thus after the ascension he was seen by Paul, who, being modest, calls himself an abortion, perceiving that he had come from repentance to being an apostle, and as not even worthy of the name, as a persecutor. But even if formerly such, yet now a teacher, having this from a gift. Even if formerly a persecutor, yet now a teacher by the gift of God, which did not exist in him in vain, since, being empowered by it, he endured more abundantly the contests for the pious faith. And the whole success which he had from choice he attributes to the grace given to him from God. If anyone says that the dead are not raised, since it is necessary that if Christ rose all rise, does he not then necessarily say that Christ has not been raised? But if he did not rise, see how many absurdities spring up: we who said this will be found false witnesses against God, even if, as you foolishly agreed to the resurrection of the Lord, yet also having seemed by faith in the one who rose to have been freed from sins, you did not cast off your sins. The one who does not accept that the soul of a human being is immortal and therefore disbelieves the resurrection, such a one is pitiable, depriving himself of eternal life, for which the saints are rich, obtaining worthy rewards. Even if some disbelieve, yet we await the resurrection, knowing that Christ has become firstfruits, resurrection of those who have fallen asleep; through which all will experience immortal life, for it follows. Since because Adam transgressed the law all those from him have died, so also in Christ, who did not know sin, they will be made alive. But some of the heretics say that only the soul of the righteous is made alive in Christ, because there is not ** for the making alive will be of all who died in Adam. As the resurrection of Christ is before all things, it will be first in honor; then in order the faithful are arranged according to the proportion of faith which they have at the coming of Christ, after which is the end, not thus distinguished toward a beginning, but that for the sake of which all the other things contributing to salvation exist, but which itself does not exist for the sake of another, being the last object of desire in itself and for itself and choiceworthy.

choices.why: The phrase is the object of the Corinthians' denial; 'resurrection' is the fixed glossary term and 'of the body' specifies what they called superfluous.
The adjective πολύθεος means 'of many gods'; 'polytheistic error' captures the false worship from which the gospel called them.
κατ' ἀλήθειαν stresses the reality of the incarnation against docetic denials; 'truly worn' keeps the verb's physical sense.
rejected: having borne a body in truth
having really put on a body

choices.why: The comparative of ἁπλοῦς refers to less sophisticated believers who might be troubled; 'simpler ones' preserves the comparative force.
Paul's self-designation; the literal sense is a miscarried or aborted fetus, which conveys his sense of unworthiness.
κατόρθωμα means a right action or achievement; 'success' fits Paul's accomplishments in ministry which he attributes to grace.

pass_b_english: Some people in Corinth were saying that the soul is mortal and that the resurrection of the body is superfluous. Paul refutes their error. Paul says: I am making known to you the gospel through which you were called out of polytheistic error to know the true God, through which you are being established and have salvation. I am making known to you the gospel of God, so that you may know that the testimony about the resurrection of the dead is not mine, nor any human being's.

The gospel was handed down to me: that the Savior came, truly took on a body, died for the sake of the resurrection of the dead, was buried, and rose. Then, so that the simpler ones may not be disturbed by the death of Christ, he adds, according to the Scriptures. For he suffered just what the prophets announced beforehand about him. Since he died, was buried, and rose, it follows that human beings will rise because of the one who rose for them, since he became the cause of their rising. If Christ is said to have died and been buried, this must be understood of his body, not his soul. Since they believed in the Savior's resurrection, they are blameworthy for not accepting along with the Savior's resurrection also the resurrection of all.

The eyewitnesses of his resurrection who are worthy of trust are those who were first with him, then five hundred. These things, he says, I hand down, which those who deceive you cannot contradict. Nevertheless, even if the dead rise, it rises incorruptible and spiritual. For this reason he did not appear to everyone, but to those he willed. So after the ascension he appeared to Paul, who in humility calls himself an untimely birth, perceiving that he came to be an apostle through repentance, and that he was not even worthy of the name because he was a persecutor. Yet even if he was once such, now he is a teacher, having this from grace.

Even if he was once a persecutor, now he is a teacher by the grace of God, which was not in him in vain, since being empowered by it he endured more abundantly the contests for the pious faith. The whole success that he had from his own choice he attributes to the grace given to him from God.

If someone says that the dead are not raised, since it is necessary that if Christ rose all rise, does he not necessarily say that Christ has not been raised either? But if he did not rise, see how many absurdities arise. We who said this will be found to be false witnesses against God, even if you foolishly agreed to the resurrection of the Lord. And even if you thought you had been freed from your sins by faith in the one who rose, you have not put away your sins.

The one who does not accept that the human soul is immortal and therefore disbelieves the resurrection is pitiable. Such a person deprives himself of eternal life, for which the saints are rich, obtaining worthy rewards. Even if some disbelieve, we await the resurrection, knowing that Christ has become the firstfruits, the resurrection of those who have fallen asleep. Through these all will experience immortal life, for it follows.

Since through Adam's transgression of the command all who are from him have died, so also in Christ, who knew no sin, they will be made alive. But some of the heretics say that only the soul of the righteous is made alive in Christ, because [text missing]. For the making alive will be of all who died in Adam.

Since Christ's resurrection is before all things, it will be first in honor. Then in order the faithful are arranged at Christ's coming according to the proportion of faith they have. After this is the end, not thus marked off as a beginning, but as that for the sake of which all other things that contribute to salvation exist, while it itself exists for the sake of nothing else, being the final object of desire, desirable for its own sake and through itself.
notes: The source contains a lacuna marked by ** after 'οὐκ ἔστιν' in the section on 1 Cor 15:21-22; the text is damaged and the missing words cannot be supplied.

problems.why: Greek 'οὕτω πρὸς ἀρχὴν διαστελλόμενον' = 'thus distinguished in relation to a beginning' or 'not marked off as a beginning.' English 'not distinguished as a beginning' misses 'οὕτω' (thus/so) and the sense. The phrase modifies 'τὸ τέλος' (the end): 'the end, not thus marked off as a beginning.' English 'not distinguished as a beginning' is unclear. The point is: the end is not a beginning, but the final goal. English 'not distinguished as a beginning' is awkward and potentially misleading—does it mean 'not distinguished from a beginning'? The Greek means 'not classified/designated as a beginning.' 'Distinguished as' is ambiguous.
problems.fix: not marked off as a beginning

problems.quote: he adds: according to the Scriptures (1 Corinthians 15:3-4)
problems.why: Parenthetical '(1 Corinthians 15:3-4)' makes it seem like Didymus cites chapter-verse, but this is editor's reference. Didymus just says 'he adds: according to the Scriptures.' The parenthetical confuses voice—makes ancient text seem modern.
problems.fix: he adds, according to the Scriptures
problems.ruling: Parenthetical '(1 Corinthians 15:3-4)' is not in source; ancient author appears to cite modern chapter-verse, misleading readers.

problems.why: The ** indicates lacuna in source; English 'because there is no **' treats ** as text rather than editorial mark for missing text. Should indicate lacuna or omit.
problems.ruling: 'because there is no **' treats editorial lacuna marker ** as translatable text, misleading readers; should indicate missing text.

problems.why: Already noted. The ** is a lacuna marker, not text to translate.
problems.ruling: Duplicate of #3; ** is editorial lacuna marker, not text. 'because there is no **' misleads readers.

problems.quote: but as that for the sake of which all other things contribute to salvation, and it itself exists for the sake of nothing else, being the final object of desire, chosen for its own sake and through itself
problems.source_quote: ἀλλὰ τὸ οὗ εἵνεκα τὰ ἄλλα πάντα τὰ συντείνοντα πρὸς σωτηρίαν, αὐτὸ δὲ οὐκ ἄλλου χάριν ὑπάρχον ἔσχατον ὀρεκτὸν καθ' ἑαυτὸ καὶ δι' ἑαυτὸ αἱρετὸν τυγχάνον
problems.why: This is extremely dense philosophical Greek, and English is barely followable. 'all other things contribute to salvation' should be 'all other things that contribute to salvation'—the relative clause is lost, making 'all other things contribute to salvation' a main clause. 'it itself exists for the sake of nothing else' is unclear. 'being the final object of desire, chosen for its own sake and through itself' piles up participles. The syntax 'but as that for the sake of which...' is broken.
problems.fix: but as that for the sake of which all other things that contribute to salvation exist, while it itself exists for the sake of nothing else, being the final object of desire, desirable for its own sake and through itself
problems.ruling: τὰ συντείνοντα πρὸς σωτηρίαν is relative clause 'things that contribute'; English 'all other things contribute' loses syntax, misrepresenting meaning.

fixed: The glossary problem about 'the soul is perishable' is real: the source uses φθαρτή (perishable) but the brief's glossary bans 'perishable' for the soul and the confirmed problem asks for consistent mortal/immortal terms. Changed to 'the soul is mortal'.

The glossary problem about 'the dead body rises' is real: the source says τὸ τεθνεὸς σῶμα ἀνίσταται, but the confirmed problem asks to standardize 'the dead' (people) vs. 'dead bodies'. Changed to 'the dead rise' to match the brief's preference.
The speaker problem is real: the English 'He says' is ambiguous between Paul and Didymus. Changed to 'Paul says' to mark the speaker clearly.
The unreadable problem about 'the law' is real: the source says τὸν νόμον, but the confirmed problem notes Adam transgressed a command, not the Torah. Changed to 'the command'.
The mistranslation problem about 'out of repentance' is real: the source says ἐκ μετανοίας, and 'through repentance' better captures the sense. Changed to 'through repentance'.

last_rejected.quote: the testimony about the resurrection of the dead is not mine, nor any human being's
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα εἰδῆτε ὅτι οὐκ ἐμή, ἀλλ' οὔ τινος ἡ περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν μνήμη
last_rejected.why: Source says 'the mention of the resurrection of the dead is not mine but no one's'; English adds 'testimony' and 'human being's', shifting sense.
last_rejected.fix: so that you may know that the mention of the resurrection of the dead is not mine, nor anyone's.
last_rejected.ruling: μνήμη can mean 'mention, record, testimony'; 'human being's' captures τινος (someone/anyone). Translation within normal semantic range.

last_rejected.quote: even if the dead body rises
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅμως, εἰ καὶ τὸ τεθνεὸς σῶμα ἀνίσταται
last_rejected.why: Greek 'τὸ τεθνεὸς σῶμα' means 'the dead body' as subject, but 'even if' suggests concession; however, the Greek states it as fact (the dead body does rise), not hypothetical. The 'even if' misrepresents the logical force—Didymus is asserting resurrection, not conceding it conditionally.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰ καί with indicative can be concessive ('even if'); translation is within normal Greek grammar range.

last_rejected.quote: even if you foolishly agreed to the resurrection of the Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰ καὶ ὡς ὑμεῖς ἠλιθίως συνέθεσθε τῇ ἐγέρσει τοῦ κυρίου
last_rejected.why: The Greek addresses hypothetical opponents ('if someone says'), not the Corinthians directly with 'you.' The 'you' here misidentifies the addressee—Paul's rhetorical target is the deniers, not the Corinthian believers whom Didymus presents as having believed.
last_rejected.fix: even if they foolishly agreed to the Lord's resurrection
last_rejected.ruling: ὑμεῖς ('you') is in the Greek source; translator faithfully renders it, not mistranslating.

last_rejected.quote: And even if you thought you had been freed from your sins by faith in the one who rose, you have not put away your sins
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ πίστει τοῦ ἀναστάντος δόξαντες ἠλευθερῶσθαι τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, οὐκ ἀπεβάλετε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν
last_rejected.why: Same issue: 'you' refers to hypothetical deniers, not the Corinthians. The rhetorical structure presents consequences for those who deny resurrection, not accusations against believers.
last_rejected.fix: and even if they thought they had been freed from their sins by faith in the one who rose, they have not put away their sins
last_rejected.ruling: ὑμῶν ('your') is in the Greek source; translator faithfully renders it, not mistranslating.

last_rejected.why: 'κατόρθωμα' means 'achievement, accomplishment, virtuous deed,' not 'success' in the modern sense. The term refers to moral/religious accomplishment, not outcome-based success.
last_rejected.ruling: κατόρθωμα can mean 'success' or 'achievement'; rendering is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: the contests for the pious faith
last_rejected.source_quote: τοὺς ἀγῶνας ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐσεβοῦς πίστεως
last_rejected.why: 'εὐσεβοῦς πίστεως' is 'the faith that is pious/godly' or 'godly faith,' not 'the pious faith' as if 'pious' modifies a definite known entity. The Greek adjective describes the quality of the faith itself.
last_rejected.ruling: 'pious faith' for εὐσεβοῦς πίστεως is standard adjective-noun rendering; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: not thus marked off as a beginning
last_rejected.why: The Greek says the end is 'not distinguished with reference to a beginning' (i.e., not defined relative to something else), not 'not marked off as a beginning.' The phrase concerns relational definition, not mistaking end for beginning.
last_rejected.fix: not thus distinguished relative to a beginning
last_rejected.ruling: πρὸς ἀρχήν can mean 'as a beginning'; rendering is defensible, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the final object of desire, desirable for its own sake and through itself
last_rejected.source_quote: ἔσχατον ὀρεκτὸν καθ' ἑαυτὸ καὶ δι' ἑαυτὸ αἱρετὸν τυγχάνον
last_rejected.why: 'ὀρεκτόν' and 'αἱρετόν' are technical philosophical terms: 'object of desire' and 'choiceworthy.' 'Desirable' for 'αἱρετόν' weakens the technical force; 'choiceworthy' or 'to be chosen' is standard.
last_rejected.fix: the final object of desire, choiceworthy for its own sake and through itself
